## Findings
- claim-1: For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), the two displayed Schur families generate \(J_v\), each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements, and graded Nakayama identifies minimality with inclusion-minimal spanning in \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\). [source-2@L1380-L1421|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1520-L1540|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: **Conditional target established.** Assume the \(p=c=1\) integral interval/Pieri presentation of task 85 and its compatible box-specialization maps. Then for every admissible \(b=\min(i,j)\ge1\) and every \(a=\min(p,c)=1\), \[ Q:=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{b+1}, \] and both proposed \(a=1\) families are minimal generating families.
## Strategy
**Conditional target established.** Let \(p=q-i\), \(c=r-j\), \(a=\min(p,c)=1\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and \(d=ij\). Assume the task-85 interval/Pieri presentation for \((p,c)=(1,1)\), and the standard Schur-basis box description of \(I_{r,q}\).

The two source-given families become exactly
\[
\mathcal F_1=\{X_k=s_{((i+1)^k,i^{j-k})}:0\le k\le b\},
\qquad
\mathcal F_2=\{Y_k=s_{(i^j,k)}:0\le k\le b\}.
\]
Indeed these are respectively the intervals from \(i^j\) to \(((i+1)^b,i^{j-b})\) and from \(i^j\) to \((i^j,b)\).

For \(p=c=1\), write
\[
C_x=P_{x,k-x}=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{j-x},k-x)}
\quad(0\le x\le k).
\]
Task 85 gives the \(h_1\)-lattice
\[
L_k=\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1}).
\]
More generally, for \(t\ge1\) and \(x\le k-t\), Pieri gives, within the interval,
\[
h_tP_{x,k-t-x}=C_x+C_{x+1}.
\]
Thus every positive-degree multiplication row lies in \(L_k\), while the \(h_1\)-rows generate \(L_k\). Hence
\[
(Q_{1,1})_{d+k}=M_{d+k}/L_k\cong\mathbb Z,
\]
with
\[
[X_k]=[C_k]=(-1)^k[C_0]=(-1)^k[Y_k].
\]
The unitriangular complementary minors from task 85 show that either endpoint is a primitive generator.

For arbitrary \(p,c\ge1\) with \(\min(p,c)=1\), the inclusion of boxes
\[
(i+1)^{j+1}\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c}
\]
gives \(I_{j+c,i+p}\subseteq I_{j+1,i+1}\), hence a quotient map
\[
\Lambda/I_{j+c,i+p}\twoheadrightarrow\Lambda/I_{j+1,i+1}.
\]
Since both \(J_{p,c}\) and \(J_{1,1}\) are generated by the same endpoint family \(\mathcal F_1\) (equivalently by \(\mathcal F_2\)), this restricts to
\[
J_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow J_{1,1},
\qquad
Q_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow Q_{1,1}.
\]
Source-backed generation implies that \(Q_{p,c}\) vanishes outside degrees \(d,\ldots,d+b\), and that \((Q_{p,c})_{d+k}\) is cyclic, generated by \([X_k]\). Its image is the primitive generator of \((Q_{1,1})_{d+k}\cong\mathbb Z\); therefore
\[
(Q_{p,c})_{d+k}\cong\mathbb Z.
\]
The same map identifies \([Y_k]=(-1)^k[X_k]\). Consequently,
\[
Q_{p,c}\cong\bigoplus_{k=0}^{b}\mathbb Z[X_k]\cong\mathbb Z^{b+1},
\]
and both \(\{\overline X_k\}\) and \(\{\overline Y_k\}\) are \(\mathbb Z\)-bases. The accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion then proves that both \(\mathcal F_1\) and \(\mathcal F_2\) are inclusion-minimal \(\Lambda\)-generating families.

## Gaps
This is conditional on the task-85 interval/Pieri presentation and on the standard Schur-basis characterization of the box ideals \(I_{r,q}\). Those hypotheses are not independently source-grounded in the supplied record. Thus no unconditional \(a=1\) theorem is claimed.

## Next
To remove the conditions, supply a proof or stable source grounding for the interval presentation and the box-ideal inclusion \(I_{j+c,i+p}\subseteq I_{j+1,i+1}\).
